Now the next logical step is to make sure that every resource the web page depends on is actually being served correctly by this local server. If any of the files are missing, have the wrong path, or are blocked for some reason, the page will fail to load correctly in the browser. I need to verify the HTTP status for each of the critical assets:

- `js/main.js` – the main application script.
- `css/style.css` – the stylesheet that defines the visual theme.
- `lib/three.module.js` – the core Three.js library.

A concise way to do this from PowerShell is to loop over the relative paths, issue a `HEAD` request with `Invoke-WebRequest` (so I only get headers, not the full content), and then output the HTTP status code together with the path. This will give me a quick checklist: each line should read `200  <path>` if everything is being served properly.

I’ll construct a `foreach` loop over an array of these five paths, invoke the `HEAD` request for each, and format the output as `"${StatusCode}  ${path}"`. This matches the style of the previous checks and will be easy to read.
